title: Get An Offer
metaTitle: Get an Offer on Your Colorado Mineral Rights
metaDescription: Request a working offer on your Colorado mineral or royalty interest, evaluated from your documents and current county activity, no obligation.
heroLead: Send us what you have on your Colorado mineral interest and we'll build an evaluation from your actual documents and current activity in your county.
intro: The fastest way to get a useful number is to send whatever you already have, a deed, a division order, a recent royalty statement, or simply the county and legal description if that's all you can locate. We'll take it from there and tell you specifically what else, if anything, would sharpen the evaluation.
There's no cost and no obligation to move forward after you receive it. Some owners use this as a first look before deciding whether to sell at all, and that's a reasonable way to use it.

sections.heading: What to include when you reach out
paragraphs: At minimum, the county where your minerals are located and your best understanding of your interest, whether that's a fraction from a deed or a decimal from a division order. If you have recent royalty statements, those give us the clearest picture of a producing interest's actual trend. If the interest is undeveloped, the legal description alone is often enough to check nearby permitting activity.

If your interest passed through inheritance and you're not entirely sure what you own, that's fine, tell us what you know and we'll help figure out the rest, including what county records or probate documents might fill in the gaps.

sections.heading: What happens after you send information
paragraphs: We review what you've provided, check it against current activity, recent permitting from the Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission for undeveloped acreage, or your production trend for producing interests, and put together a working range along with an explanation of how we arrived at it.
If we need more information to firm up the number, we'll tell you specifically what's missing rather than asking for a vague pile of paperwork. Most owners can gather what's needed within a few days.

sections.heading: Colorado-specific factors we account for
paragraphs: If your minerals sit in a split-estate situation, meaning you don't own the surface, we factor that into how we evaluate development potential, since it affects how a surface-use agreement would need to be negotiated separately. We also account for current setback rules, which shape where new wells can practically be sited near your tract.
None of this changes the basic process, it just means the evaluation reflects your actual situation rather than a generic statewide assumption.

sections.heading: No pressure, no rushed deadlines
paragraphs: We won't ask you to sign anything on a short deadline, and there's no penalty for taking time to review an offer, compare it against your own records, or talk to your own advisor before deciding. Mineral interests don't have a narrow window where value disappears overnight.
If you decide to move forward, the next step is title review, and we'll walk you through what that involves before you commit to anything.

sections.heading: If your interest has never been formally evaluated before
paragraphs: It's common to reach out with only a vague sense of what you own, a family name, a county, maybe an old letter mentioning oil and gas. We can usually work backward from that starting point, checking county records and, if the interest is producing, tracking down which operator is currently paying royalties on it.

This kind of first-time evaluation takes a little longer than one for an owner with organized records, but it's a normal part of what we do, and it's often the owners in this position who benefit most from finally having a clear number to work from.

faqs.question: Is there a cost to get an offer?
faqs.answer: No, requesting an evaluation is free and doesn't obligate you to sell.

faqs.question: What if I don't have any documents on hand?
faqs.answer: Send us what you remember, the county and roughly how the interest came to you, and we can help identify what records exist and where to find them.

faqs.question: How quickly can I get a working number?
faqs.answer: It depends on how complete your information is, but many owners get a preliminary range within a few business days of sending documents.

faqs.question: Can I get an offer on just part of my interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, partial sales are common, whether that's a fraction of your ownership or specific depths while retaining the rest.

faqs.question: What if I'm not sure whether I want to sell yet?
faqs.answer: That's fine. Many owners request an evaluation to have a number in hand before deciding, with no obligation to act on it.

faqs.question: Can I get an offer if I only own a small fractional interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, small fractional interests are common in Colorado's older mineral estates and are evaluated the same way, off actual production or nearby activity, regardless of the size of the fraction.

faqs.question: Will you explain how you reached the number, or just give me a figure?
faqs.answer: We'll walk through what informed it, your production trend or nearby permitting activity, so you understand the reasoning rather than just receiving a dollar figure.

faqs.question: Can I request an offer for a family member who isn't able to reach out themselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, just let us know your relationship and how you're helping, and we can work with you on gathering the needed information.
